name: Kevin Hern

issue_poll.name: Centiment / University of Oklahoma (Allyson Shortle) poll for News 9, May 2026, 457 registered Oklahoma Republicans (top issues, up to three choices)
issue_poll.note: No 2026 Oklahoma poll of the full general electorate ranking issues was found; this Republican-only pre-primary poll is the only 2026 state poll with a full ranked issue list. Top 10 taken in poll order, except 'Protecting conservative values' (15%, tied 9th-10th) was dropped as not vote-testable and replaced by the next issue, Second Amendment rights (11%).

issues.detail: Lower costs for Americans through the Trump agenda
Reduce regulations; bring manufacturing back from overseas; advocate for Oklahoma infrastructure investment
Build border barriers and other border-security measures
Expand school choice, including broader allowed uses of 529 accounts
Address crime in cities; reduce illegal drugs entering the country
Pass a constitutional balanced-budget amendment; extend the existing tax cuts
Make it easier for businesses to offer affordable health insurance; lower premiums
Enact term limits for members of Congress
Supports returning oil refining to the U.S.

plan_caveats: Issue poll covers registered Republicans only (May 2026, pre-primary), not the general electorate; no ranked general-election issue poll for Oklahoma in 2026 was found.
Campaign site (hernforsenate.com) could not be fetched; its priorities are taken from News 9's Oct 2, 2026 candidate summary, which cites the site.
No general-election debate or detailed issue interview was found; Hern did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 survey. Most 2026 statements were framed as supporting the Trump agenda without specifics.
Term limits rated Concrete (clear end state) although the source does not say whether he means a constitutional amendment or the number of terms; judgment call.
Education rated Partial: '529 expansion' named but which uses would be added is unstated.
Health care rated Vague: Dec 2025 remarks opposing extended ACA subsidies predate his Senate candidacy and were excluded; 2026 remarks named only goals.
Energy: only a general comment at a March 2026 campaign stop; his House energy work is past record and excluded.
Term start: Oklahoma AG opinion indicates the Nov 3 winner may take office on certification, before Jan 3, 2027 (appointee Alan Armstrong holds the seat until then); standard term dates kept.
